components.note: 成 (chéng) is a sound clue for 城 chéng, 诚 chéng and 盛 chéng: the same sound.
人 (person) — a side-view figure of a person walking. As a radical it appears as 亻 on the left: 你 他 们.

example.hanzi: 在这个国家,十八岁就被视为成人。
example.pinyin: zài zhège guójiā, shíbā suì jiù bèi shìwéi chéngrén.
example.english: In this country, eighteen is considered the age of adulthood.
example.fact: The legal age of adulthood varies widely across the world — Scotland has historically set the age for many legal contracts at just 16, while Japan lowered its age of adult majority from 20 to 18 only as recently as 2022, showing how much this line is a social choice rather than a fixed biological one.

examples.hanzi: 这家书店有成人书籍，也有儿童书籍。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā shūdiàn yǒu chéngrén shūjí, yě yǒu értóng shūjí.
examples.english: This bookstore has both adult books and children's books.

examples.hanzi: 孩子成人以后，就要学会独立。
examples.pinyin: Háizi chéngrén yǐhòu, jiù yào xuéhuì dúlì.
examples.english: After growing up, a child has to learn to be independent.

components.note: 木 (wood) — trees and wooden things: 树, 板, 样; 模 was a wooden mold or pattern.
莫 (mò) is close to mó; same part in 摸 mō, 膜 mó, 墓 mù.
弋 (yì) is a loose sound clue for shì; 弋 also in 试 shì and 拭 shì.
工 (work, craft) — a craftsman's pattern, a standard.

example.hanzi: 这家公司正在尝试一种全新的商业模式。
example.pinyin: zhè jiā gōngsī zhèngzài chángshì yī zhǒng quánxīn de shāngyè móshì.
example.english: This company is trying out a brand-new business model.
example.fact: Netflix's original business model in 1997 was DVD-by-mail rental with no late fees, a pattern that seemed radical against Blockbuster's late-fee-dependent stores — Blockbuster actually turned down a chance to buy Netflix for $50 million in 2000 and filed for bankruptcy just eleven years later.

examples.hanzi: 手机可以切换成静音模式。
examples.pinyin: Shǒujī kěyǐ qiēhuàn chéng jìngyīn móshì.
examples.english: The phone can be switched to silent mode.

examples.hanzi: 每个人都有自己的学习模式。
examples.pinyin: Měi gè rén dōu yǒu zìjǐ de xuéxí móshì.
examples.english: Everyone has their own learning pattern.

components.note: 鸟 (bird) — marks birds, as in 鸭 duck, 鹅 goose, 鸽 pigeon; 鸡 is a chicken. 又 only replaces the old sound part.
肉 — a picture of a slab of meat with its grain lines; as a left-hand radical it shrinks to ⺼ in 脸, 腿, 肌.

example.hanzi: 这道菜用的是新鲜的鸡肉和青椒。
example.pinyin: zhè dào cài yòng de shì xīnxiān de jīròu hé qīngjiāo.
example.english: This dish uses fresh chicken and green peppers.
example.fact: Chickens are the most numerous bird on the planet, with an estimated global population exceeding 25 billion at any given time — outnumbering humans by more than three to one — and archaeologists trace their domestication from wild red junglefowl in Southeast Asia back at least 3,500 years.

examples.hanzi: 我不吃猪肉，但是吃鸡肉。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ bù chī zhūròu, dànshì chī jīròu.
examples.english: I don't eat pork, but I eat chicken.

examples.hanzi: 鸡肉沙拉是一道很健康的菜。
examples.pinyin: Jīròu shālā shì yí dào hěn jiànkāng de cài.
examples.english: Chicken salad is a very healthy dish.

components.note: 攵 (tap, hand with stick) — actions applied to people: 放, 改, 政; 教 is to teach, traditionally with a rod.
孝 (xiào) is a near sound match for jiào; also in 酵 jiào.
师 (shī) is a sound clue for 狮 shī (lion) and 筛 shāi; as a word it means master or teacher.

example.hanzi: 这位教师在乡村小学教了三十年书。
example.pinyin: zhè wèi jiàoshī zài xiāngcūn xiǎoxué jiāole sānshí nián shū.
example.english: This teacher taught at a rural elementary school for thirty years.
example.fact: Finland, often cited as having one of the world's most effective education systems, requires all primary school teachers to hold a master's degree and accepts fewer than 10% of applicants into its teacher training programs, treating the profession with a selectivity comparable to medicine or law in many other countries.

examples.hanzi: 她的梦想是成为一名教师。
examples.pinyin: Tā de mèngxiǎng shì chéngwéi yì míng jiàoshī.
examples.english: Her dream is to become a teacher.

examples.hanzi: 九月十日是中国的教师节。
examples.pinyin: Jiǔ yuè shí rì shì Zhōngguó de Jiàoshījié.
examples.english: September 10 is Teachers' Day in China.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — marks actions done by hand, as in 打, 推, 按; 抗 is to resist or hold off.
亢 (kàng) gives the sound exactly: 抗 kàng, also in 炕 kàng.

example.hanzi: 人民起来抗议这项政策。
example.pinyin: Rénmín qǐlái kàngyì zhè xiàng zhèngcè.
example.english: The people rose up to protest this policy.
example.fact: 抗 is 'to resist': 抗议 (protest), 对抗 (to oppose), 抗体 (antibody), 抗生素 (antibiotic) and 抗战, the 'war of resistance' against Japan. It is also a prefix like 'anti-', as in 抗病毒.

examples.hanzi: 多运动能增强身体的抵抗力。
examples.pinyin: Duō yùndòng néng zēngqiáng shēntǐ de dǐkànglì.
examples.english: Exercising more strengthens your body's resistance.

examples.hanzi: 医生给他用了抗生素。
examples.pinyin: Yīshēng gěi tā yòng le kàngshēngsù.
examples.english: The doctor gave him antibiotics.

components.note: 中 (middle) — a line through the middle of a box, a centre mark. 中 gives sound to 钟 zhōng, 种 zhǒng, 忠 zhōng and 衷 zhōng.
士 (scholar, soldier) — usually read as an axe or weapon, so a warrior or gentleman (士兵, 博士). Memory aid: 士 has the longer bar on top, 土 (earth) on the bottom.

example.hanzi: 那位中士带领新兵进行了体能训练。
example.pinyin: nà wèi zhōngshì dàilǐng xīnbīng jìnxíngle tǐnéng xùnliàn.
example.english: That sergeant led the new recruits through physical training.
example.fact: The chevron insignia used to denote sergeant rank in many modern militaries originated in medieval heraldry, where the inverted-V shape symbolized a roof rafter or protection, and was formally adopted by the British Army in 1802 to visually distinguish non-commissioned officers on the battlefield.

examples.hanzi: 他在部队里当了五年中士。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài bùduì lǐ dāng le wǔ nián zhōngshì.
examples.english: He served as a sergeant in the army for five years.

examples.hanzi: 中士向长官敬了一个礼。
examples.pinyin: Zhōngshì xiàng zhǎngguān jìng le yí gè lǐ.
examples.english: The sergeant saluted his commanding officer.

components.note: 心 (heart) — marks the mind and feelings, as in 想, 思, 意; 忽 is a lapse of attention, hence neglect or suddenly.
勿 (wù) is a loose hint for hū; 物 wù shares it.
各 (gè) is only a loose hint for lüè; 路 lù and 络 luò share it.

example.hanzi: 我们不能忽略气候变化带来的长期影响。
example.pinyin: wǒmen bùnéng hūlüè qìhòu biànhuà dàilái de chángqī yǐngxiǎng.
example.english: We cannot ignore the long-term effects brought by climate change.
example.fact: The Keeling Curve, a continuous record of atmospheric carbon dioxide measured atop Mauna Loa in Hawaii since 1958, is one of the longest unbroken environmental datasets in existence and was nearly defunded multiple times in its early decades before its long-term significance for tracking climate change was widely recognized.

examples.hanzi: 他太着急了，忽略了一个重要的细节。
examples.pinyin: Tā tài zháojí le, hūlüè le yí gè zhòngyào de xìjié.
examples.english: He was too anxious and overlooked an important detail.

examples.hanzi: 别忽略孩子的感受。
examples.pinyin: Bié hūlüè háizi de gǎnshòu.
examples.english: Don't ignore the child's feelings.

components.note: 風 (traditional wind) — 风 is the simplified form of 風, which had 凡 (fán) as a loose sound hint around 虫; the simplified shape is just a reduced form.
日 (sun) — 日 is the sun — 暴 originally meant to expose to the sun (still in 暴露), then violent, as in 暴力.

example.hanzi: 一场巨大的风暴摧毁了整个渔村。
example.pinyin: yī chǎng jùdà de fēngbào cuīhuǐle zhěnggè yúcūn.
example.english: A huge storm destroyed the entire fishing village.
example.fact: Typhoon Tip, which formed over the Pacific Ocean in October 1979, remains the largest tropical cyclone ever recorded, with a diameter of about 2,220 kilometers — roughly the size of the continental United States east of the Mississippi — though its size did not translate into the highest wind speeds ever measured.

examples.hanzi: 海上的风暴让船不得不返回港口。
examples.pinyin: Hǎishàng de fēngbào ràng chuán bùdébù fǎnhuí gǎngkǒu.
examples.english: The storm at sea forced the ship to return to port.

examples.hanzi: 这起丑闻引发了一场舆论风暴。
examples.pinyin: Zhè qǐ chǒuwén yǐnfā le yì chǎng yúlùn fēngbào.
examples.english: This scandal set off a storm of public opinion.

components.note: 土 (earth) — earth radical — a base is something solid on the ground, as in 地, 城, 块.
其 (qí) — loose hint — 基 is jī; 其 also sounds out 期 qī and 旗 qí.
于 (yú) is a sound clue for 宇 yǔ and 芋 yù; it is a light grammar word meaning "at, to".

example.hanzi: 这个决定是基于大量的市场调查数据做出的。
example.pinyin: zhège juédìng shì jīyú dàliàng de shìchǎng diàochá shùjù zuòchū de.
example.english: This decision was made based on a large amount of market research data.
example.fact: The Richter scale, developed by Charles Richter in 1935, is based on a logarithmic formula in which each whole-number increase represents roughly 31.6 times more energy release — meaning a magnitude 7 earthquake releases about a thousand times more energy than a magnitude 5, not just two units' worth.

examples.hanzi: 基于以上原因，我们决定推迟会议。
examples.pinyin: Jīyú yǐshàng yuányīn, wǒmen juédìng tuīchí huìyì.
examples.english: Based on the above reasons, we decided to postpone the meeting.

examples.hanzi: 这个软件是基于开源代码开发的。
examples.pinyin: Zhège ruǎnjiàn shì jīyú kāiyuán dàimǎ kāifā de.
examples.english: This software was developed on the basis of open-source code.

components.note: 西 (west) — traditionally a bird settling on its nest at sunset, hence west; 西 turns up in 要 and 栖.
阝 on the right is 邑 (city) — places, as in 都 capital, 邮 post, 那: a district or ministry.
咅 (pǒu) is a loose sound clue for bù; 咅 also in 剖 pōu, 培 péi and 陪 péi.

example.hanzi: 淘金热吸引了大批移民前往美国西部。
example.pinyin: táojīnrè xīyǐnle dàpī yímín qiánwǎng měiguó xībù.
example.english: The gold rush attracted large numbers of immigrants to the American West.
example.fact: The California Gold Rush that began in 1848 drew roughly 300,000 people to the American West within a few years, transforming San Francisco from a settlement of about 1,000 residents into a city of 25,000 by 1850 — one of the fastest urban growth rates in recorded history.

examples.hanzi: 中国西部有很多美丽的草原和高山。
examples.pinyin: Zhōngguó xībù yǒu hěn duō měilì de cǎoyuán hé gāoshān.
examples.english: The west of China has many beautiful grasslands and high mountains.

examples.hanzi: 我下个月要去美国西部旅行。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xià gè yuè yào qù Měiguó xībù lǚxíng.
examples.english: Next month I'm traveling to the western United States.

components.note: 页 (head, page) — marks the head and face, as in 顶, 题, 顺; 预 is thinking ahead.
予 (yǔ) hints at the sound: 预 yù is close, as in 豫 yù.
氵 (water radical, 三点水) — water: 河, 深, 浅; 测 was measuring the depth of water.
则 (zé) is close to cè; same part in 侧 cè and 厕 cè.

example.hanzi: 气象局预测明天将有大雨。
example.pinyin: qìxiàngjú yùcè míngtiān jiāng yǒu dàyǔ.
example.english: The weather bureau predicts heavy rain tomorrow.
example.fact: Modern weather forecasting owes much of its accuracy to Edward Lorenz's 1961 discovery of chaos theory, when he found that rounding a computer's atmospheric simulation input from six decimal places to three produced wildly different long-term weather predictions — the origin of the popular "butterfly effect" metaphor.

examples.hanzi: 没有人能准确预测股市的变化。
examples.pinyin: Méiyǒu rén néng zhǔnquè yùcè gǔshì de biànhuà.
examples.english: No one can accurately predict changes in the stock market.

examples.hanzi: 专家的预测和实际情况差不多。
examples.pinyin: Zhuānjiā de yùcè hé shíjì qíngkuàng chàbuduō.
examples.english: The experts' forecast was close to what actually happened.

components.note: 一 (one) — a single horizontal stroke is the number one; 二 and 三 just add strokes, so the first three numbers are tally marks.
阝 (hill, from 阜) — marks slopes and ranks, as in 院, 阶, 防; 阵 is a battle formation.
车 (chariot) — war chariots lined up in rows.

example.hanzi: 窗外突然传来一阵急促的敲门声。
example.pinyin: chuāng wài tūrán chuánlái yī zhèn jícù de qiāomén shēng.
example.english: A burst of urgent knocking suddenly came from outside the window.
example.fact: Woodpeckers can peck a tree at over 20 times per second during a single burst, and their skulls have evolved a spongy bone structure and a tongue that wraps around the brain like a seatbelt to absorb the shock — decelerating each strike fast enough that it would otherwise cause a concussion in most other animals.

examples.hanzi: 一阵风吹过，树叶沙沙作响。
examples.pinyin: Yízhèn fēng chuīguò, shùyè shāshā zuòxiǎng.
examples.english: A gust of wind blew by and the leaves rustled.

examples.hanzi: 听到这个消息，他心里一阵难过。
examples.pinyin: Tīngdào zhège xiāoxi, tā xīnlǐ yízhèn nánguò.
examples.english: Hearing this news, he felt a wave of sadness.

components.note: 尹 (to govern, a hand holding a staff) — the ruler; also in 伊 and 群 qún.
口 (mouth) — the ruler issues commands; 君 also sounds out 群 qún and 裙 qún.

example.hanzi: 国君下令修建新桥。
example.pinyin: Guójūn xiàlìng xiūjiàn xīn qiáo.
example.english: The king ordered a new bridge to be built.
example.fact: 君 is the ruler, and by extension a refined person: 君子 (a gentleman in the Confucian sense). Today it can also be an affectionate suffix after a name, like the Japanese -kun, such as 小明君.

examples.hanzi: 他是一位谦谦君子。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì yí wèi qiānqiān jūnzǐ.
examples.english: He is a modest and refined gentleman.

examples.hanzi: 古代的君王要听大臣的意见。
examples.pinyin: Gǔdài de jūnwáng yào tīng dàchén de yìjiàn.
examples.english: Ancient monarchs had to listen to their ministers.

components.note: 亻 (person) — person radical — 优 first meant a person who performs or is excellent, in 演员 and 优秀.
尤 (yóu) — near sound — 优 is yōu; 尤 also sounds out 忧 yōu.
隹 (short-tailed bird) — marks birds, as in 难, 谁 (loan uses), 集; 雅 first named a crow, now borrowed for 'elegant'.
牙 (yá) hints at the sound: 雅 yǎ is close to 鸦 yā and 呀 ya.

example.hanzi: 她的舞蹈动作非常优雅。
example.pinyin: Tā de wǔdǎo dòngzuò fēicháng yōuyǎ.
example.english: Her dance movements are very graceful.
example.fact: Flamingos sleep standing on one leg not for balance but to conserve body heat, since a leg tucked up against the body loses far less warmth than one planted in cold water. Studies of flamingo posture found they hold this stance even when asleep and unbalanced by wind, suggesting it costs them almost no extra effort.

examples.hanzi: 她说话的声音很优雅。
examples.pinyin: Tā shuōhuà de shēngyīn hěn yōuyǎ.
examples.english: Her voice is very graceful.

examples.hanzi: 这家咖啡馆的环境优雅安静。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā kāfēiguǎn de huánjìng yōuyǎ ānjìng.
examples.english: This café has an elegant and quiet atmosphere.

components.note: 夕 (evening) — the left part, the time-of-day family as in 夜, 多, 梦. Memory aid: things done at night are outside the ordinary.
卜 (divination) — Dictionary story: night 夕 divination 卜, strange and 'outside'. A hedged mnemonic: 外面 outside, 另外 in addition.
衣 (clothes; 衤 on the left) — the outer garment.
毛 (fur) — a fur coat worn outside: the outside, the surface, then to show.

example.hanzi: 不要只看一个人的外表。
example.pinyin: Bùyào zhǐ kàn yí gè rén de wàibiǎo.
example.english: Don't just judge a person by their outward appearance.
example.fact: The mimic octopus, first documented off Indonesia in the late 1990s, can imitate the shape, color, and even movement style of more than a dozen other sea creatures, including lionfish, sea snakes, and flatfish. Marine biologists believe it switches disguises depending on which predator is nearby, choosing whichever appearance best deters that specific threat.

examples.hanzi: 他外表很冷，其实人很热心。
examples.pinyin: Tā wàibiǎo hěn lěng, qíshí rén hěn rèxīn.
examples.english: He looks cold on the outside, but is actually very warm-hearted.

examples.hanzi: 这个水果外表不好看，但很甜。
examples.pinyin: Zhège shuǐguǒ wàibiǎo bù hǎokàn, dàn hěn tián.
examples.english: This fruit doesn't look good on the outside but it is very sweet.

components.note: 土 (earth) — marks soil and dust, as in 地, 城, 墙; 埃 is fine dust.
矣 (yǐ) is a loose hint for āi; 唉 āi and 挨 āi share the part.
及 (reach) — a hand 又 catching up with a person from behind: to reach, then and; seen in 以及, 及时.

example.hanzi: 埃及有许多古老的金字塔。
example.pinyin: Āijí yǒu xǔduō gǔlǎo de jīnzìtǎ.
example.english: Egypt has many ancient pyramids.
example.fact: The Great Pyramid of Giza, completed around 2560 BC, remained the tallest human-made structure on Earth for almost 3,800 years — a record unbroken until England's Lincoln Cathedral surpassed it in 1311. Egyptologists estimate it originally stood about 146 meters tall before its outer casing stones were stripped away over the centuries.

examples.hanzi: 我一直想去埃及看金字塔。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ yìzhí xiǎng qù Āijí kàn jīnzìtǎ.
examples.english: I've always wanted to go to Egypt to see the pyramids.

examples.hanzi: 埃及的夏天非常热。
examples.pinyin: Āijí de xiàtiān fēicháng rè.
examples.english: Summers in Egypt are very hot.

components.note: 巾 (cloth) — marks cloth, as in 布, 带, 帽; 幕 is a curtain or screen.
莫 (mò) hints at the sound: 幕 mù is close to 墓 mù, 慕 mù and 暮 mù.
后 (after, behind) — two words merged in simplified writing: old 后 "ruler" (皇后 empress) and 後 "behind, later" (as in 然后).

example.hanzi: 很多幕后工作人员从未被观众看到。
example.pinyin: Hěn duō mùhòu gōngzuò rényuán cóngwèi bèi guānzhòng kàndào.
example.english: Many behind-the-scenes staff are never seen by the audience.
example.fact: A single minute of footage in a modern animated film can take a studio's rendering farm hundreds, even thousands, of computer-hours to produce, because every frame's lighting, shadows, and textures are calculated separately before being stitched into motion. Pixar's render farm for its early films already used thousands of processors running around the clock just to keep up with release schedules.

examples.hanzi: 这场演出的幕后故事很有趣。
examples.pinyin: Zhè chǎng yǎnchū de mùhòu gùshi hěn yǒuqù.
examples.english: The behind-the-scenes story of this show is very interesting.

examples.hanzi: 他一直在幕后默默地支持我们。
examples.pinyin: Tā yìzhí zài mùhòu mòmò de zhīchí wǒmen.
examples.english: He has been quietly supporting us behind the scenes all along.

components.note: 小 (small) — three small dots, tiny grains. As a radical it appears in 少 few, 尖 sharp.
彐 (hand-like part) — 事 is usually explained as a hand holding a tool or tally, 'handling business' — a hedged reading, not certain.
史 (history, scribe) — shares an ancient root with 事: a hand holding a recording tool. Both are about handling official 'matters'.

example.hanzi: 别为这点小事生气。
example.pinyin: Bié wèi zhè diǎn xiǎoshì shēngqì.
example.english: Don't get angry over such a trivial matter.
example.fact: The 'butterfly effect,' named by meteorologist Edward Lorenz in the 1960s, describes how an extremely small change in initial conditions — like the flap of a butterfly's wings — can, in a chaotic system, theoretically alter the path of a weather system weeks later. Lorenz discovered the idea by accident, when rounding a weather-model input by a tiny fraction produced a wildly different forecast.

examples.hanzi: 这只是一件小事，不用放在心上。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhǐshì yí jiàn xiǎoshì, búyòng fàng zài xīn shàng.
examples.english: It's just a small matter; don't take it to heart.

examples.hanzi: 夫妻之间常常因为小事吵架。
examples.pinyin: Fūqī zhījiān chángcháng yīnwèi xiǎoshì chǎojià.
examples.english: Couples often quarrel over trivial things.

components.note: 犭 (dog, beast) — animals: 狗, 猫, 狼; 独 first meant a solitary animal, then alone.
The old sound part 蜀 (shǔ) is also in 属 shǔ, 烛 zhú and 触 chù; simplified 独 shows 虫 instead.
牛 (ox) — cattle and animals, as in 物 thing, 牧 herd, 牺 sacrifice: 特 first meant a bull, then special.
寺 (sì) is only a loose sound clue for tè; 寺 also in 诗 shī and 持 chí.

example.hanzi: 每个人的指纹都是独特的。
example.pinyin: Měi gè rén de zhǐwén dōu shì dútè de.
example.english: Everyone's fingerprint is unique.
example.fact: No two people's fingerprints are exactly alike, not even those of identical twins, because the ridge patterns form partly from random pressure and movement of the fetus against the walls of the amniotic sac in the womb, not from genetics alone. This is why twins who share identical DNA can still be distinguished at a crime scene by fingerprint alone.

examples.hanzi: 这家店的咖啡味道很独特。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā diàn de kāfēi wèidao hěn dútè.
examples.english: The coffee at this shop has a very distinctive flavor.

examples.hanzi: 她有自己独特的穿衣风格。
examples.pinyin: Tā yǒu zìjǐ dútè de chuān yī fēnggé.
examples.english: She has her own unique style of dressing.

components.note: 氵 (water) — water, as in 河, 海, 清: in the old form 灋, water stood for fairness, so law and method.
医 (doctor) — simplified from 醫, which had 酉 (medicinal wine, as in 酒) at the bottom; the box 匚 and arrow 矢 remain.

example.hanzi: 法医通过尸检确定了死亡时间。
example.pinyin: Fǎyī tōngguò shījiǎn quèdìngle sǐwáng shíjiān.
example.english: The forensic pathologist determined the time of death through an autopsy.
example.fact: Forensic entomologists can estimate how long a body has been deceased by studying which insect species have colonized it, since blowflies typically arrive within minutes of death and different species succeed one another in a fairly predictable order over the following weeks. This branch of forensic science, sometimes called 'the maggot's timeline,' has been used as courtroom evidence since the late 19th century.

examples.hanzi: 她是一名法医，每天都要处理很多案件。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì yì míng fǎyī, měi tiān dōu yào chǔlǐ hěn duō ànjiàn.
examples.english: She is a forensic doctor and handles many cases every day.

examples.hanzi: 法医在现场发现了重要的线索。
examples.pinyin: Fǎyī zài xiànchǎng fāxiàn le zhòngyào de xiànsuǒ.
examples.english: The forensic examiner found important clues at the scene.

components.note: 艹 (plants) — marks grasses and herbs, as in 花, 草, 茶; 苏 originally named the perilla plant, and is also short for Jiangsu and Soviet (苏联).

example.hanzi: 苏州是一座美丽的城市。
example.pinyin: Sūzhōu shì yí zuò měilì de chéngshì.
example.english: Suzhou is a beautiful city.
example.fact: 苏 abbreviates 江苏 (Jiangsu) and 苏州 (Suzhou), famous in the saying 上有天堂，下有苏杭 ('Heaven above, Suzhou and Hangzhou below'). It is also a surname (the poet 苏轼) and means 'revive' in 复苏.

examples.hanzi: 他的老家在江苏。
examples.pinyin: Tā de lǎojiā zài Jiāngsū.
examples.english: His hometown is in Jiangsu.

examples.hanzi: 苏老师今天请假了。
examples.pinyin: Sū lǎoshī jīntiān qǐngjià le.
examples.english: Teacher Su is on leave today.

components.note: 页 (head) — marks the head and face, as in 顶, 题, 顺; 额 is the forehead, then an amount.
客 (kè) is a loose hint for é; 格 gé and 路 lù share it.
夕 (evening) — the left part, the time-of-day family as in 夜, 多, 梦. Memory aid: things done at night are outside the ordinary.
卜 (divination) — Dictionary story: night 夕 divination 卜, strange and 'outside'. A hedged mnemonic: 外面 outside, 另外 in addition.

example.hanzi: 这次旅行需要一些额外的费用。
example.pinyin: Zhè cì lǚxíng xūyào yìxiē éwài de fèiyòng.
example.english: This trip requires some additional costs.
example.fact: Budget airlines pioneered 'unbundling' airfares in the 2000s, separating the base ticket price from checked bags, seat selection, and priority boarding. Ryanair has reported years where its average base fare was priced below the airline's actual per-passenger fuel cost, with most of its profit coming entirely from these extra add-on fees.

examples.hanzi: 加班的话，公司会给额外的补助。
examples.pinyin: Jiābān de huà, gōngsī huì gěi éwài de bǔzhù.
examples.english: If you work overtime, the company gives extra allowance.

examples.hanzi: 我不想给你添额外的麻烦。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ bù xiǎng gěi nǐ tiān éwài de máfan.
examples.english: I don't want to cause you additional trouble.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — speech, as in 吃, 唱, 问: voices in unison. 同 also gives sound to 铜 tóng, 桶 tǒng, 洞 dòng.
一 (one) — a single horizontal stroke is the number one; 二 and 三 just add strokes, so the first three numbers are tally marks.
人 (person) — the top part. 个 is the general measure word, as in 一个, 这个, 那个.
丨 (a vertical tally) — under 人, read as one tally mark per person: counting individuals one by one.

example.hanzi: 我们两个人喜欢同一个电影。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen liǎng gè rén xǐhuan tóng yí gè diànyǐng.
example.english: The two of us like the same movie.
example.fact: Nearly every cell in the human body is replaced over time — skin cells last only a couple of weeks, red blood cells about four months, and most of the body's cells are estimated to turn over within roughly seven to ten years. Philosophers often connect this to the ancient Ship of Theseus paradox: if all the parts are eventually swapped out, is it still 'the same' body?

examples.hanzi: 我和她在同一个公司上班。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ hé tā zài tóng yí gè gōngsī shàngbān.
examples.english: She and I work at the same company.

examples.hanzi: 他们住在同一个小区里。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen zhù zài tóng yí gè xiǎoqū lǐ.
examples.english: They live in the same neighborhood.

components.note: 干 (dry; do) — a forked pole or shield. It lends its sound to 肝 gān, 杆 gān, 赶 gǎn, 汗 hàn and 岸 àn.
扌 (hand radical, 提手旁) — actions by hand: 打, 拉, 推; 扰 is to stir up and disturb.
尤 (yóu) is only a loose sound hint for rǎo.

example.hanzi: 手机信号受到了干扰。
example.pinyin: Shǒujī xìnhào shòudàole gānrǎo.
example.english: The phone signal was interfered with.
example.fact: In 1964, Bell Labs engineers Arno Penzias and Robert Wilson were trying to eliminate a mysterious background noise picked up by their radio antenna, at first suspecting pigeon droppings on the equipment. The interference turned out to be the cosmic microwave background — leftover radiation from the Big Bang — a discovery that earned them the Nobel Prize in Physics.

examples.hanzi: 请不要干扰别人学习。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng búyào gānrǎo biéren xuéxí.
examples.english: Please don't disturb others who are studying.

examples.hanzi: 外面的噪音干扰了他的思考。
examples.pinyin: Wàimiàn de zàoyīn gānrǎo le tā de sīkǎo.
examples.english: The noise outside disrupted his thinking.

components.note: 氵 (water) — marks water and sinking, as in 海, 没 sink, 游; 沉 is to sink.
冗 (rǒng) is only a loose sound hint for chén.

example.hanzi: 这个箱子太沉了，我搬不动。
example.pinyin: Zhège xiāngzi tài chén le, wǒ bān bú dòng.
example.english: This box is too heavy; I can't move it.
example.fact: 沉 means 'to sink' (下沉), and colloquially 'heavy': 这个箱子很沉. It also describes states: 沉默 (silent), 沉重 (heavy, serious) and 沉睡 (deep sleep).

examples.hanzi: 石头沉到水底去了。
examples.pinyin: Shítou chén dào shuǐdǐ qù le.
examples.english: The stone sank to the bottom of the water.

examples.hanzi: 他沉默了很久。
examples.pinyin: Tā chénmò le hěn jiǔ.
examples.english: He was silent for a long time.

components.note: 冫 (ice) — marks cold and reduction, as in 冰, 冷, 冻; 减 is to lessen.
咸 (xián) hints at the sound: 减 jiǎn is close to 感 gǎn, 喊 hǎn and 碱 jiǎn.
小 (small) — a 小 with a stroke taken off: not much. 少 also gives sound to 沙 shā, 抄 chāo and 炒 chǎo.

example.hanzi: 医生建议他减少盐的摄入量。
example.pinyin: Yīshēng jiànyì tā jiǎnshǎo yán de shèrùliàng.
example.english: The doctor recommended he reduce his salt intake.
example.fact: After the 1987 Montreal Protocol phased out ozone-depleting chemicals worldwide, satellite measurements show the Antarctic ozone hole has been gradually shrinking year over year. Atmospheric scientists project it could fully recover to 1980 levels by around the 2060s, making the treaty one of the most successful environmental agreements in history.

examples.hanzi: 这个城市的汽车尾气正在逐渐减少。
examples.pinyin: Zhège chéngshì de qìchē wěiqì zhèngzài zhújiàn jiǎnshǎo.
examples.english: Car exhaust in this city is gradually decreasing.

examples.hanzi: 我想减少看手机的时间。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng jiǎnshǎo kàn shǒujī de shíjiān.
examples.english: I want to cut down the time I spend on my phone.

meanings: rent for a room or house

components.note: 户 (door) — doors and houses, as in 所 and 扇: a room with a door.
方 (fāng) is a close sound clue for fáng; 方 also sounds out 放 fàng and 访 fǎng.
禾 (grain) — 禾 is grain — rent was originally paid in grain, as in 种 plant, 秋 autumn.
且 (qiě) — loose hint — 租 is zū; 且 also sounds out 组 zǔ and 祖 zǔ.

example.hanzi: 这个城市的房租一年比一年贵。
example.pinyin: Zhège chéngshì de fángzū yì nián bǐ yì nián guì.
example.english: Rent in this city gets more expensive every year.
example.fact: In ancient Rome, most residents didn't own their homes but rented cramped upper floors of apartment blocks called insulae. These buildings were often thrown up quickly and cheaply, and some were known to collapse, prompting Emperor Augustus to cap building heights at roughly 20 meters to reduce the risk.

examples.hanzi: 我每个月要交三千块的房租。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ měi gè yuè yào jiāo sān qiān kuài de fángzū.
examples.english: I have to pay three thousand yuan in rent every month.

examples.hanzi: 房东说下个月要涨房租。
examples.pinyin: Fángdōng shuō xià gè yuè yào zhǎng fángzū.
examples.english: The landlord said the rent will go up next month.

components.note: 囗 (enclosure) — borders and walls, as in 园 garden, 圆 round, 回 return; 囗 is the country's boundary.
玉 (jade) — treasure within the border; the traditional 國 had 或 (defended territory) inside.
会 (meet, can) — simplified from 會, a lid on a container: bringing things together; hence meeting, then "can" (huì).

example.hanzi: 国会今天通过了一项新法律。
example.pinyin: Guóhuì jīntiān tōngguòle yí xiàng xīn fǎlǜ.
example.english: Congress passed a new law today.
example.fact: The U.S. Capitol's dome, completed in 1866, is made of cast iron rather than stone, using more than 8.9 million kilograms of it. Architects chose the lightweight, fireproof material because the original masonry dome could not have safely supported the much taller, more ornate structure topped by the Statue of Freedom.

examples.hanzi: 国会议员们正在讨论这个提案。
examples.pinyin: Guóhuì yìyuánmen zhèngzài tǎolùn zhège tí'àn.
examples.english: Members of parliament are discussing this proposal.

examples.hanzi: 总统要在国会上发表讲话。
examples.pinyin: Zǒngtǒng yào zài guóhuì shàng fābiǎo jiǎnghuà.
examples.english: The president will give a speech in Congress.

components.note: 亻 (person) — people, as in 你, 他, 做: 作 is something a person does or makes.
乍 (zuò) gives the exact sound; 乍 also in 昨 zuó, 炸 zhà and 怎 zěn.
木 (tree) — wood, as in 桌, 树, 板: 案 is a wooden table.
安 (ān) is a close sound clue for àn; also in 按 àn.

example.hanzi: 警方正在调查他作案的动机。
example.pinyin: Jǐngfāng zhèngzài diàochá tā zuò'àn de dòngjī.
example.english: Police are investigating his motive for committing the crime.
example.fact: The first criminal conviction based on DNA evidence came in 1988 in the UK, when genetic fingerprinting linked Colin Pitchfork to two murders. The same technique has since exonerated hundreds of wrongly convicted people worldwide through post-conviction DNA testing programs.

examples.hanzi: 小偷作案的时候被监控拍到了。
examples.pinyin: Xiǎotōu zuò'àn de shíhou bèi jiānkòng pāi dào le.
examples.english: The thief was caught on camera while committing the crime.

examples.hanzi: 警察怀疑他有作案的时间。
examples.pinyin: Jǐngchá huáiyí tā yǒu zuò'àn de shíjiān.
examples.english: The police suspect he had the time to commit the crime.

components.note: 阝 (hill, from 阜) — marks slopes and barriers, as in 院, 阶, 障; 防 is a dike to guard against floods, then to defend.
方 (fāng) gives the sound: 防 fáng is close, as in 房 fáng and 妨 fáng.
宀 (roof) — a house or shelter, as in 家 home, 安 safe, 完; a hand 寸 under a roof means guarding.
寸 (hand, inch) — originally a hand, as in 对, 寻, 封.

example.hanzi: 这支球队的防守非常出色。
example.pinyin: Zhè zhī qiúduì de fángshǒu fēicháng chūsè.
example.english: This team's defense is outstanding.
example.fact: The Great Wall of China was never a single continuous wall but a network of walls, watchtowers, and forts built by different dynasties over more than 2,000 years. Modern surveys using satellite and infrared imaging put the combined length of all its branches at roughly 21,000 kilometers.

examples.hanzi: 我们的球队今天主要以防守为主。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen de qiúduì jīntiān zhǔyào yǐ fángshǒu wéi zhǔ.
examples.english: Our team is mainly playing defensively today.

examples.hanzi: 士兵们在城墙上防守了三天三夜。
examples.pinyin: Shìbīngmen zài chéngqiáng shàng fángshǒu le sān tiān sān yè.
examples.english: The soldiers defended the city wall for three days and nights.

components.note: 欠 (open mouth) — 欠 shows an open mouth, as in 吹, 歌, 欢; 欺 is deceiving by speech.
其 (qí) — near sound — 欺 is qī; 其 also sounds out 期 qī and 旗 qí.
贝 (cowry shell, money) — wealth and value: 财, 货, 买, 贵. 负 shows a person 人 carrying money: a burden, to bear or owe.

example.hanzi: 老师制止了那个欺负同学的男孩。
example.pinyin: Lǎoshī zhìzhǐle nàge qīfù tóngxué de nánhái.
example.english: The teacher stopped the boy who was bullying his classmate.
example.fact: The term 'pecking order' comes directly from observations of chickens. In the 1920s, Norwegian zoologist Thorleif Schjelderup-Ebbe documented how hens establish a strict dominance hierarchy through repeated pecking, with each bird learning exactly who it can peck and who it must submit to.

examples.hanzi: 哥哥经常欺负弟弟，妈妈很生气。
examples.pinyin: Gēge jīngcháng qīfu dìdi, māma hěn shēngqì.
examples.english: The older brother often bullies his younger brother, and Mom is angry.

examples.hanzi: 如果有人欺负你，一定要告诉老师。
examples.pinyin: Rúguǒ yǒu rén qīfu nǐ, yídìng yào gàosu lǎoshī.
examples.english: If anyone bullies you, be sure to tell the teacher.

components.note: 田 (field) — a picture of a field divided into plots. Appears in 男 man (field + strength), 界 border, 留 stay.

example.hanzi: 农民在田里种水稻。
example.pinyin: Nóngmín zài tián lǐ zhòng shuǐdào.
example.english: The farmers are growing rice in the fields.
example.fact: 田 is a field: 农田, 水田 (paddy), 田野 (open country). 田径 is 'track and field'. 田 is also a common surname.

examples.hanzi: 这片田里种满了玉米。
examples.pinyin: Zhè piàn tián li zhòng mǎn le yùmǐ.
examples.english: This field is full of corn.

examples.hanzi: 他在农田里干活。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài nóngtián li gànhuó.
examples.english: He is working in the farmland.

components.note: 牛 (ox) — leading an ox by a rope; as a part, 牛 marks cattle and animals, as in 物 thing, 特 special, 牧 herd.

example.hanzi: 他牵着孩子的手过马路。
example.pinyin: Tā qiān zhe háizi de shǒu guò mǎlù.
example.english: He led the child across the road by the hand.
example.fact: 牵 is leading by a rope and, by extension, by the hand: 牵手 (hold hands). It also gives 牵挂 ('to worry about, a heart tugged') and 牵涉 (to involve). 牵牛花 is the morning glory.

examples.hanzi: 小狗被主人牵着走。
examples.pinyin: Xiǎo gǒu bèi zhǔrén qiān zhe zǒu.
examples.english: The puppy is being led by its owner.

examples.hanzi: 他们手牵手走在街上。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen shǒu qiān shǒu zǒu zài jiē shang.
examples.english: They walk down the street hand in hand.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — marks actions done by hand, as in 打, 拉, 提; 挽 is to pull or draw back.
免 (miǎn) hints at the sound: 挽 wǎn is close to 晚 wǎn.
攵 (tap, hand with stick) — actions taken on something: 教, 放, 改; 救 is to take action to rescue.
求 (qiú) is a near sound match for jiù; 求 also means ask for help.

example.hanzi: 医生的及时抢救挽救了他的生命。
example.pinyin: Yīshēng de jíshí qiǎngjiù wǎnjiùle tā de shēngmìng.
example.english: The doctor's timely rescue saved his life.
example.fact: CPR as it's known today wasn't standardized until 1960, when researchers combined mouth-to-mouth rescue breathing with chest compressions. Before that, 19th-century rescuers tried far stranger methods on drowning victims, including rolling them over barrels or swinging them by the ankles to force water out of the lungs.

examples.hanzi: 这个婚姻已经没办法挽救了。
examples.pinyin: Zhège hūnyīn yǐjīng méi bànfǎ wǎnjiù le.
examples.english: There's no way to save this marriage.

examples.hanzi: 他们想尽办法挽救濒临倒闭的公司。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen xiǎng jìn bànfǎ wǎnjiù bīnlín dǎobì de gōngsī.
examples.english: They tried everything to rescue the company on the verge of collapse.

components.note: 攵 (tap, strike) — 攵 marks an action, here counting; as in 教, 放.
娄 (lóu) — loose hint — 数 is shù; 娄 also sounds out 楼 lóu.
扌 (hand) — hand actions, as in 打, 拿, 抱: to grip or rely on.
居 (jū) is a close sound clue for jù; 居 also in 剧 jù and 锯 jù.
广 (building) — marks halls and shelters, as in 店, 座, 床; 库 is a storehouse, here for carts 车.

example.hanzi: 所有的用户信息都存储在数据库里。
example.pinyin: Suǒyǒu de yònghù xìnxī dōu cúnchú zài shùjùkù lǐ.
example.english: All user information is stored in the database.
example.fact: The relational database model, still the backbone of most software today, was introduced by IBM researcher Edgar F. Codd in a 1970 paper. The idea was initially considered impractical, and IBM itself was reluctant to build it commercially for fear of undercutting its existing database products.

examples.hanzi: 程序员正在更新公司的数据库。
examples.pinyin: Chéngxùyuán zhèngzài gēngxīn gōngsī de shùjùkù.
examples.english: The programmer is updating the company's database.

examples.hanzi: 这个数据库里有上百万条记录。
examples.pinyin: Zhège shùjùkù lǐ yǒu shàng bǎi wàn tiáo jìlù.
examples.english: This database has millions of records.

components.note: 亻 (person) — people, as in 你, 他, 做: 体 is a person's body.
本 (root) — the root of a person, the body; the traditional form was 體 with 骨 (bone).
会 (meet, can) — simplified from 會, a lid on a container: bringing things together; hence meeting, then "can" (huì).

example.hanzi: 只有亲身经历才能真正体会那种感觉。
example.pinyin: Zhǐyǒu qīnshēn jīnglì cáinéng zhēnzhèng tǐhuì nà zhǒng gǎnjué.
example.english: Only through personal experience can one truly understand that feeling.
example.fact: Mirror neurons, discovered in the 1990s by Italian researchers studying macaque monkeys, fire both when an animal performs an action and when it merely watches another perform the same action. The finding is often cited as a possible biological basis for empathy, since it may let a brain partially simulate another creature's experience.

examples.hanzi: 出国以后，我才体会到家的重要。
examples.pinyin: Chūguó yǐhòu, wǒ cái tǐhuì dào jiā de zhòngyào.
examples.english: Only after going abroad did I realize how important home is.

examples.hanzi: 读完这本书，我有很深的体会。
examples.pinyin: Dú wán zhè běn shū, wǒ yǒu hěn shēn de tǐhuì.
examples.english: After finishing this book, I gained a deep understanding.

meanings: to give birth to a child

components.note: 土 (earth) — a green shoot pushing up from the ground: growth, birth, life. 生 also sounds out 性 xìng, 姓 xìng and 星 xīng.
生 (birth) — traditional 產 was 生 (birth) topped by 彦 for sound; the idea is giving birth, so bringing forth, as in 生产 and 产生.

example.hanzi: 这家工厂每天生产上千件产品。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiā gōngchǎng měitiān shēngchǎn shàngqiān jiàn chǎnpǐn.
example.english: This factory produces thousands of products every day.
example.fact: Henry Ford didn't invent the assembly line, but his 1913 moving line for the Model T cut the time needed to build a car from roughly 12 hours down to about 93 minutes. The change helped transform automobiles from an expensive luxury into a product ordinary American workers could afford.

examples.hanzi: 这家工厂主要生产汽车零件。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā gōngchǎng zhǔyào shēngchǎn qìchē língjiàn.
examples.english: This factory mainly produces car parts.

examples.hanzi: 她下个月就要生产了。
examples.pinyin: Tā xià gè yuè jiù yào shēngchǎn le.
examples.english: She is due to give birth next month.

components.note: 上 (above) — a mark above a line, the mirror of 下 below.
台 (tái) as a sound part appears in 抬 tái, 胎 tāi, 苔 tái, and also in 治 zhì and 始 shǐ.

example.hanzi: 演员紧张地走上台去。
example.pinyin: Yǎnyuán jǐnzhāng de zǒu shàngtái qù.
example.english: The actor nervously walked onto the stage.
example.fact: Ancient Greek theaters, such as the Theatre of Epidaurus built around 300 BC, were engineered with such precise acoustics that a whisper or a dropped coin on stage can reportedly be heard clearly from the back row, some 60 meters away. Acoustic engineers still study its stone seating rows to understand how the shape filters out low-frequency crowd noise while carrying higher-pitched voices.

examples.hanzi: 下一个上台的是我们班的同学。
examples.pinyin: Xià yí gè shàngtái de shì wǒmen bān de tóngxué.
examples.english: The next person on stage is a classmate from our class.

examples.hanzi: 他上台领奖的时候特别激动。
examples.pinyin: Tā shàngtái lǐngjiǎng de shíhou tèbié jīdòng.
examples.english: He was extremely excited when he went on stage to receive the award.

components.note: ⺼ (flesh, from 肉) — marks body parts, as in 肚 belly, 脸 face, 腿 leg; 腰 is the waist.
要 (yào) — close sound: 腰 yāo. 要 was originally a picture of a waist.

example.hanzi: 我的腰有点疼。
example.pinyin: Wǒ de yāo yǒudiǎn téng.
example.english: My lower back hurts a bit.
example.fact: 腰 covers both the waist and the lower back, so 腰疼 usually means a back ache. 腰带 is a belt and 腰包 a waist pouch; 腰 can also be the waist of trousers.

examples.hanzi: 他弯下腰系鞋带。
examples.pinyin: Tā wān xià yāo jì xiédài.
examples.english: He bent down to tie his shoelaces.

examples.hanzi: 我腰酸背痛,想休息一下。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ yāosuān bèitòng, xiǎng xiūxi yíxià.
examples.english: My back aches; I want to rest a bit.

components.note: 一 (one) — a single horizontal stroke is the number one; 二 and 三 just add strokes, so the first three numbers are tally marks.
萬 (traditional ten thousand) — 万 is the simplified form of 萬, which pictured a scorpion borrowed for the number 10,000; 万 also sounds out 迈 mài.

example.hanzi: 这台电脑花了他一万块钱。
example.pinyin: Zhè tái diànnǎo huāle tā yī wàn kuài qián.
example.english: This computer cost him ten thousand yuan.
example.fact: A single teaspoon of healthy soil can contain up to ten thousand different microbial species, according to soil ecologists — a level of hidden biodiversity that researchers now compare in scale to that of a tropical rainforest. Most of these species have never been cultured or formally identified in a lab.

examples.hanzi: 这个体育场可以坐一万个观众。
examples.pinyin: Zhège tǐyùchǎng kěyǐ zuò yí wàn gè guānzhòng.
examples.english: This stadium can seat ten thousand spectators.

examples.hanzi: 他一个月的工资有一万多。
examples.pinyin: Tā yí gè yuè de gōngzī yǒu yí wàn duō.
examples.english: His monthly salary is over ten thousand.

components.note: 行 (go, road) — 行 (walk, go) splits around the middle — 街 is a road; compare 往 go and 衔.
圭 (guī) — loose hint only — 街 is jiē.
辶 (walk) — movement and roads, as in 这 this, 过 pass, 近 near; a 道 is a road, then a way or principle.
首 (shǒu, head) is only a loose sound hint for dào; 首 also means "head/first", fitting a lead-the-way road.

example.hanzi: 春节期间街道上挂满了红灯笼。
example.pinyin: Chūnjié qījiān jiēdào shàng guà mǎnle hóng dēnglóng.
example.english: During Spring Festival the streets are hung with red lanterns.
example.fact: Ancient Rome's road network eventually spanned more than 400,000 kilometers, with about 80,500 kilometers of it paved in stone. The system was built so precisely that many modern European highways still trace the exact routes the Romans laid out over two thousand years ago.

examples.hanzi: 这条街道很干净，两边都是树。
examples.pinyin: Zhè tiáo jiēdào hěn gānjìng, liǎngbiān dōu shì shù.
examples.english: This street is very clean, with trees on both sides.

examples.hanzi: 街道办事处负责办理居民的证明。
examples.pinyin: Jiēdào bànshìchù fùzé bànlǐ jūmín de zhèngmíng.
examples.english: The subdistrict office handles residents' certificates.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — hand radical — 播 is scattering seed by hand, then broadcasting.
番 (fān) — near sound — 播 is bō; 番 also sounds out 翻 fān and 潘 pān.
攵 (tap, strike) — hand with stick, as in 教, 收, 改: to drive away, set free.
方 (fāng) is a close sound clue for fàng; 方 also in 房 fáng and 访 fǎng.

example.hanzi: 电视台正在播放一场足球比赛。
example.pinyin: Diànshìtái zhèngzài bòfàng yì chǎng zúqiú bǐsài.
example.english: The TV station is broadcasting a soccer match.
example.fact: The first regular television broadcasts began in the UK in 1936 via the BBC, using a mechanical scanning system that could only manage about 30 lines of picture resolution. That's roughly a fraction of the detail found in even a low-end modern smartphone screen.

examples.hanzi: 电台每天晚上播放轻音乐。
examples.pinyin: Diàntái měi tiān wǎnshang bōfàng qīng yīnyuè.
examples.english: The radio station plays light music every evening.

examples.hanzi: 请播放一下上次会议的录音。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng bōfàng yíxià shàng cì huìyì de lùyīn.
examples.english: Please play the recording of the last meeting.

components.note: 氵 (water, 三点水) — marks water and liquids, as in 海 sea, 河 river, 汤 soup; 泥 is mud or clay, wet earth.
尼 (ní) — same sound: 泥 ní. 尼 also sounds out 呢 ne and 妮 nī.

example.hanzi: 孩子们在泥里玩得很开心。
example.pinyin: Háizimen zài ní lǐ wán de hěn kāixīn.
example.english: The kids are having a great time playing in the mud.
example.fact: 泥 is the everyday word for mud and clay, and it appears in 水泥 (cement, literally "water mud"), 泥土 and 泥巴. A rarer reading nì means "to plaster," but ní is the one you will meet constantly.

examples.hanzi: 他的新鞋上沾满了泥。
examples.pinyin: Tā de xīnxié shang zhān mǎn le ní.
examples.english: His new shoes are covered in mud.

examples.hanzi: 他喜欢用黏土和泥巴做东西。
examples.pinyin: Tā xǐhuan yòng niántǔ hé níba zuò dōngxi.
examples.english: He likes making things with clay and mud.

components.note: 大 (big) — a front-facing person with arms and legs spread wide: big. As radical, 大 is in 天 sky, 太 too much, 夫 man.
氵 (water) — 氵 is water, as in 河, 汤, 酒; 海 is the sea.
每 (měi) — near sound — 海 is hǎi; 每 also sounds out 梅 méi and 悔 huǐ.

example.hanzi: 他站在悬崖上眺望着大海。
example.pinyin: Tā zhàn zài xuányá shàng tiàowàngzhe dàhǎi.
example.english: He stood on the cliff gazing at the sea.
example.fact: More than 80 percent of the ocean remains unmapped and unexplored, and scientists estimate humans have directly observed less than one-tenth of one percent of the deep seafloor. In practical terms, we currently have more detailed maps of the surface of the Moon and Mars than of our own ocean floor.

examples.hanzi: 夏天我最喜欢去大海边游泳。
examples.pinyin: Xiàtiān wǒ zuì xǐhuan qù dàhǎi biān yóuyǒng.
examples.english: In summer I like going swimming at the sea the most.

examples.hanzi: 大海一望无际，让人心胸开阔。
examples.pinyin: Dàhǎi yí wàng wújì, ràng rén xīnxiōng kāikuò.
examples.english: The sea stretches boundlessly and broadens one's mind.

components.note: 医 (doctor) — simplified from 醫, which had 酉 (medicinal wine, as in 酒) at the bottom; the box 匚 and arrow 矢 remain.
师 (shī) is a sound clue for 狮 shī (lion) and 筛 shāi; as a word it means master or teacher.

example.hanzi: 这位医师在乡村工作了三十年。
example.pinyin: Zhè wèi yīshī zài xiāngcūn gōngzuòle sānshí nián.
example.english: This physician has worked in the countryside for thirty years.
example.fact: The Hippocratic Oath, traditionally attributed to the Greek physician Hippocrates around the 5th century BC, never actually contains the exact phrase 'first, do no harm.' That precise wording was popularized centuries later by other writers, even though the sentiment closely echoes the oath's original pledges.

examples.hanzi: 他想考一个执业医师资格证。
examples.pinyin: Tā xiǎng kǎo yí gè zhíyè yīshī zīgézhèng.
examples.english: He wants to get a practicing physician's license.

examples.hanzi: 这位医师对每个病人都很耐心。
examples.pinyin: Zhè wèi yīshī duì měi gè bìngrén dōu hěn nàixīn.
examples.english: This doctor is patient with every patient.

components.note: 月 (flesh) — ⺼ is the body radical (月 in 脸, 脑); 脱 is slipping off a layer, like skin or clothes.
兑 (duì) — near sound — 脱 is tuō; 兑 also sounds out 说 shuō and 税 shuì.
離 (traditional) — 隹 (bird) plus 离 as sound (lí). 离 was an old name for a mythical beast, so the 'leave' sense comes from 離; 离 kept only the sound part.

example.hanzi: 火箭成功脱离了地球的引力。
example.pinyin: Huǒjiàn chénggōng tuōlíle dìqiú de yǐnlì.
example.english: The rocket successfully broke free of Earth's gravity.
example.fact: To break completely free of Earth's gravity, a spacecraft must reach roughly 11.2 kilometers per second, known as escape velocity — about 33 times the speed of sound. That is why rockets burn the vast majority of their fuel in just the first few minutes after launch.

examples.hanzi: 病人已经脱离了生命危险。
examples.pinyin: Bìngrén yǐjīng tuōlí le shēngmìng wēixiǎn.
examples.english: The patient is out of danger.

examples.hanzi: 我们不能脱离实际来讨论问题。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen bù néng tuōlí shíjì lái tǎolùn wèntí.
examples.english: We can't discuss the issue divorced from reality.

components.note: 酉 (wine jar) — marks liquor, as in 酒, 醉, 醒; 酗 is drunken rowdiness.
凶 (xiōng) hints at the sound: 酗 xù is close; 凶 also means fierce.
酉 (wine jar) — fermented drinks and flavors: 醉 drunk, 醒 sober, 酸 sour, 配 match; 酒 is liquor, with 氵 for the liquid.
酉 also hints at the sound: yǒu is close to jiǔ.

example.hanzi: 长期酗酒对肝脏损害很大。
example.pinyin: Chángqī xùjiǔ duì gānzàng sǔnhài hěn dà.
example.english: Long-term excessive drinking severely damages the liver.
example.fact: The human liver is one of the few organs capable of regenerating itself — even after up to 70 percent of its tissue is removed or damaged, it can regrow to nearly its original size within a few months. Chronic alcohol abuse, however, can eventually overwhelm this capacity and cause irreversible scarring known as cirrhosis.

examples.hanzi: 他因为酗酒丢掉了工作。
examples.pinyin: Tā yīnwèi xùjiǔ diūdiào le gōngzuò.
examples.english: He lost his job because of excessive drinking.

examples.hanzi: 医生劝他不要再酗酒了。
examples.pinyin: Yīshēng quàn tā búyào zài xùjiǔ le.
examples.english: The doctor urged him to stop drinking to excess.

components.note: 火 (fire) — fire above a person (儿 legs) — a person carrying fire gives light; 光 is bright and shining, as in 阳光, 时光.
儿 (legs, person) — the bottom 儿 is a walking person, seen also in 先, 兄, 元.
日 (sun) — the sun beside the moon: two light sources, so bright and clear.
月 (moon) — as in 朋, 期, 有; here it brightens the night.

example.hanzi: 他对未来充满光明的希望。
example.pinyin: Tā duì wèilái chōngmǎn guāngmíng de xīwàng.
example.english: He is full of bright hope for the future.
example.fact: Light from the Sun takes about 8 minutes and 20 seconds to reach Earth, so if the Sun suddenly vanished, observers on Earth would keep seeing it shine in the sky for more than eight more minutes before the sky went dark.

examples.hanzi: 走出隧道，眼前一片光明。
examples.pinyin: Zǒuchū suìdào, yǎnqián yí piàn guāngmíng.
examples.english: Coming out of the tunnel, everything ahead was bright.

examples.hanzi: 他是个光明正大的人，从不说谎。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì gè guāngmíngzhèngdà de rén, cóng bù shuōhuǎng.
examples.english: He is an open and upright person who never lies.

components.note: 贝 (shell, old money) — marks money and trade, as in 财, 货, 贵; 贷 is to lend or borrow.
代 (dài) gives the sound exactly: 贷 dài, also in 袋 dài.
欠 (open mouth, owe) — marks wanting and owing, as in 歌, 欢, 欲; 款 is a sum owed or paid.

example.hanzi: 他向银行申请了一笔贷款买房。
example.pinyin: Tā xiàng yínháng shēnqǐngle yì bǐ dàikuǎn mǎi fáng.
example.english: He applied for a loan from the bank to buy a house.
example.fact: Economist Muhammad Yunus founded Grameen Bank in Bangladesh in 1983 to offer small 'microloans' to people too poor to qualify for traditional bank credit, without requiring any collateral. The model spread to dozens of countries and eventually earned Yunus the Nobel Peace Prize in 2006.

examples.hanzi: 我们买房子贷款了一百万。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen mǎi fángzi dàikuǎn le yì bǎi wàn.
examples.english: We took out a loan of one million to buy the house.

examples.hanzi: 银行同意给他们公司贷款。
examples.pinyin: Yínháng tóngyì gěi tāmen gōngsī dàikuǎn.
examples.english: The bank agreed to lend money to their company.

components.note: 此 (cǐ) is a sound clue for 紫 zǐ, 雌 cí and 些 xiē; as a word it means "this".
刂 (knife) — cutting and sharpness: 利, 别, 到; 刻 is to carve, and the carved marks on a clock became quarter hours.
亥 (hài) is only a loose sound hint; same part in 孩 hái and 核 hé.

example.hanzi: 此刻，全场观众都安静下来。
example.pinyin: Cǐkè, quánchǎng guānzhòng dōu ānjìng xiàlái.
example.english: At this moment, the whole audience fell silent.
example.fact: Neuroscientists estimate that the brain's felt sense of an immediate 'now' actually spans a window of only about two to three seconds, sometimes called the 'psychological present.' Everything experienced as happening right now is, technically, a brief stretch of already-processed sensory information.

examples.hanzi: 此刻我心里特别平静。
examples.pinyin: Cǐkè wǒ xīnlǐ tèbié píngjìng.
examples.english: At this moment I feel especially calm.

examples.hanzi: 他想起了此刻远在家乡的妈妈。
examples.pinyin: Tā xiǎngqǐ le cǐkè yuǎn zài jiāxiāng de māma.
examples.english: He thought of his mother, who at this moment is far away in his hometown.
